observations: Photo 0 shows a small aluminum-cast worm-gear type speed reducer/gearbox, isolated on a wood/cardboard surface.
Output flange has a hollow shaft bore with four bolt holes arranged radially.
Input side shows cooling fins typical of a worm-drive housing, with a small bore for a motor shaft coupling.
A watermark reads 'POSTED ON JIJI / STEVE INDUSTRIAL' — this is the seller's listing watermark, not a manufacturer brand or model plate.
No manufacturer name, model number, ratio, or capacity markings are visible or legible anywhere on the casting.
No motor is attached; only the reducer housing/gearbox itself is shown.
Surface shows some light oxidation/dust but no visible cracks, chips, or leaks from this angle.
Only one photo, one angle — opposite side, nameplate (if any), shaft ends, and interior gearing are not shown.

claims.claim: This is a motor speed reducer
claims.evidence: photo 0 shows a housing consistent with a worm-gear speed reducer (input fin section, output flange with hollow bore)

risks.risk: Internal gear/worm condition (wear, stripped teeth, lubrication state) cannot be seen from outside
risks.proof: Video of input shaft being turned by hand showing smooth output rotation, or photo with cover removed showing gear teeth
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed working / possible internal wear

risks.risk: No ratio, torque, or size markings visible, which strongly affects value
risks.proof: Close-up photo of any stamped nameplate or casting markings on the body
risks.if_unproven: priced at generic small-reducer worst case, lowest plausible spec

risks.risk: Missing nameplate could mean a generic/unbranded unit rather than a known-brand gearbox
risks.proof: Photo of any brand plate or stamped logo on the casting

risks.risk: Shaft bore size/key-way compatibility unknown, limits buyer's ability to match to existing motor
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the output shaft bore with a ruler or caliper for scale
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown-fit, buyer assumes adaptation risk

risks.risk: Possible hidden corrosion, cracks, or oil leakage on the unseen side/base
risks.proof: Photos of the reverse side, underside, and any seals
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly damaged until shown clean

proof_requests: Close-up of any nameplate or stamped model/ratio markings on the housing
Photo of the reverse side and underside of the unit
Short video of the input shaft being turned by hand to show the output shaft moves freely and smoothly
Close-up of the output shaft bore and keyway with a ruler for scale
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a worm-gear speed reducer housing, but with no legible brand/model/ratio and no proof of working internals, it must be priced at the worst-case generic, unverified-condition level.
